director.chapterArc: High-tension survival through tactical reversal to paralyzing grief.
director.restraintNote: Maintain adult observational distance; let silence carry the weight of death rather than vocalizing it.

cues.delivery: Internal dissociation; counting is a rhythmic anchor against panic. Do not rush the count.
cues.from: His father held the bend for two minutes.
cues.through: Toren knew afterward that it had been about two minutes, because he had been counting, and he never stopped being able to count it. Two minutes. He would meet people, later, who assumed it must have been longer, and he never corrected them, because correcting them meant explaining that he had been counting.
cues.reason: Establishes Toren's fractured mental state and the passage of time.

cues.delivery: Clinical description of violence. Focus on mechanics (knee height, arcs) rather than gore.
cues.from: Garrick Voss went into the bend with a brush axe, which is a farm tool with a hooked head on a four-foot haft, made for cutting saplings off at the root, and he cut. He did not do anything fancy. He put his back against the rock on the eastern side so nothing could get behind him, and he worked the axe in short flat arcs at the height of a man's knee, and the husks came at him one and two at a time because that was all the width the bend allowed, and they went down at the knee, and he stepped on them.
cues.through: Toren stood eight feet behind him and to the left with the crooked spike out, and killed the ones that got past, and there were not many, and he was so frightened that his hearing had gone strange — everything arriving a half second late and slightly too loud.
cues.reason: Grounds the scene in physical reality before emotional escalation.

cues.delivery: Sharp command from Garrick. No rising inflection; pure urgency.
cues.through: Wyck and Milo had the cart moving again. Dessa had Pitch. Senna was flat in the bed with the blankets over her and one hand knotted in the side rail.

cues.delivery: Toren's obedience is physical. Describe the violence against Senna with detached precision.
cues.from: He got on the far side. He didn't want to. He did it because his father's voice had a thing in it that made your legs obey before your opinion arrived.
cues.through: Senna did not scream. She got her arm up. She was seventy-three years old and there was almost nothing left of her and she got her arm up between it and her throat, and it opened her forearm and her shoulder, and then Wyck hit it off her with a length of rebar he had been carrying since Sallow Creek for exactly no reason at all, and it went over the side, and Wyck hit it again on the ground, and then twice more after it had stopped moving.
cues.reason: Contrast between Toren's paralysis and Wyck's brutal efficiency.

cues.delivery: Marta is calm but breathless. Her voice must sound strained by exertion.
cues.from: Marta came up the side of the cart. She had one hand out behind her holding the wall, and she put the other flat on Senna's shoulder, and the blood slowed. It did not stop. It slowed, the way water slows when someone upstream shuts a gate part of the way.
cues.through: She said it perfectly calmly. Then she turned around to face back down the cut, because her wall had gone thin enough to see through, and she was the only one who could hold it, and she was standing on the road with her boots planted and her back to the guardrail.
cues.reason: Establishes the cost of her magic before she collapses.

cues.delivery: Toren's realization. Slow down significantly; the 'three steps' are a lifetime.
cues.from: Toren saw it happen, and it was three steps away, and he could not get there. He would go over those three steps for the rest of his life, and there was never any version of them where he got there.
cues.through: Marta Faust went down under it, and the wall went out like a lamp, and Milo made a sound that Toren had no name for and did not let go of his grandmother's shoulder, because his mother had told him not to.
cues.reason: The moment of failure and Marta's death.

cues.delivery: Shift to the stranger. Describe his impossible movement with wonder suppressed; treat it as a physical fact.
cues.from: Then the noise from the north changed.
cues.through: The husks did what husks do. They went at him, all of them, straight and fast and without any interest in what had happened to the one in front.
cues.reason: The tactical reversal that breaks Toren's understanding of Ember mechanics.

cues.delivery: Taren's internal analysis. The stranger is 'clearing a drain,' not fighting heroically.
cues.from: He killed eleven in about nine seconds, and it was not impressive. That was the strangest part. There was nothing showy in it at all. He killed them the way Bram Sark had split them, economically, at the knee and the hip, only faster and without ever quite stopping moving, and his face while he did it was the face of a man clearing a blocked drain.
cues.through: He did Marta's thing, Toren thought. He did Marta's thing and he did my father's thing and he did them in the same minute and he isn't even looking at us.
cues.reason: Reinforces the economy of violence and the strangeness of dual Ember use.

cues.delivery: The stranger's command. Toren is frozen; the pause in his speech reflects shock.
cues.from: "You," said the man. He had not turned around. "Boy with the Ember. What's ahead of you? North. In the bend."
cues.through: "Then get the cart north and go through the bend and don't stop in it," he said. "I can hold one end. Do you understand what I'm telling you? One end."
cues.reason: Establishes the new hierarchy and the immediate tactical need.

cues.delivery: Garrick's return. His voice is clipped; the physical description of his injury must be stark.
cues.from: His father came out of the bend.
cues.through: The bend was open. That was what his father had spent two minutes buying, and Toren did not understand until much later that his father had been standing in it after it was already won, on legs that had stopped being able to carry him anywhere else, waiting for somebody to come and take the road off him.

cues.delivery: Toren runs but is ineffective. The stranger demands a choice.
cues.from: The cart went for it. Dessa had Pitch's head down and was hauling him bodily, and Wyck was at the wheel, and Milo was still in the bed with both hands on Senna's shoulder and his face turned away from where his mother had been, and Toren ran alongside with the spike out and killed one more, poorly, on the third try.
cues.reason: The climax of the action sequence.

cues.delivery: Toren's forced combat. The 'unearned' second of confidence must be undercut by the fall.
cues.through: Toren went at it before it finished getting up, and did not think about the shape, and put the crooked spike through it under the arm the way he had the first one, and it came apart, and he had one enormous and entirely unearned second of believing he was the sort of person this happened easily for.

cues.delivery: Rook's intervention. The 'road cracked' moment is a physical release of tension.
cues.from: The second one landed on him from behind.
cues.through: The fourth one reached the cart bed and got one arm over the side rail before Milo Faust — who had not lifted his hands off Senna's shoulder, who did not lift them then — kicked it in the head twice with both heels and screamed at it until Wyck got there.
cues.reason: The stranger saves Toren but exposes the rear guard.

cues.delivery: Aftermath. The dust settling and Rook collecting fuel must be slow and rhythmic.
cues.from: And the pinch shut again behind all of it, wall to rail, and stayed shut.
cues.through: The man walked back down the line of it with a flat tin flask and crouched at each of the good seams and drew it up into the flask with two fingers, unhurried, the way you'd skim cream.
cues.reason: Transition from violence to grim utility.

cues.delivery: Rook's assessment. His voice is flat; the news about Senna must land with finality.
cues.from: He did four before he said anything.
cues.through: "Of course you are," the man said, and something in his voice closed.
cues.reason: The realization that they are alone and time has run out.

cues.delivery: Toren's paralysis. The final paragraph must be heavy; the Ember is cold.
cues.from: He straightened up and looked at them properly for the first time, and Toren watched him count.
cues.through: Toren stood in the middle of the road with his father's Ember gone cold and slack in his fist and the disk hanging under his shirt where nobody could see it, and did not go with the man, and did not go around the bend, and could not make his legs do either thing.
cues.reason: The emotional landing of grief and numbness.

He would meet people, later, who assumed it must have been longer, and he never corrected them, because correcting them meant explaining that he had been counting.
pauses.reason: Allow the weight of 'two minutes' to settle before moving to action.

pauses.reason: Brief breath after establishing Toren's sensory distortion.

pauses.reason: Pause for the brutality of Wyck's action and Senna's injury to register.

pauses.reason: Major reset after Marta turns her back; a moment of dread before she falls.

pauses.reason: Emotional landing on Marta's death and Milo's silence. Let the horror sit.

pauses.after: He did Marta's thing, Toren thought. He did Marta's thing and he did my father's thing and he did them in the same minute and he isn't even looking at us.
pauses.reason: Pause for Toren to process the impossibility of what he just saw (dual Ember use).

pauses.after: "Then get the cart north and go through the bend and don't stop in it," he said. "I can hold one end. Do you understand what I'm telling you? One end."
pauses.reason: Time for the command 'One end' to be understood by both character and listener.

pauses.reason: Pause after Garrick's realization that he must stay; a moment of tragic clarity.

pauses.after: He went down hard on his front with the whole weight of it across his shoulders, and the spike went out — out, gone, a grey stone in his fist under his own chest — and he could not get his arm free and could not roll and he had time to understand, with awful precision, that this was going to be how it happened.
pauses.reason: Brief pause before the road cracks and Rook intervenes.

pauses.after: And the pinch shut again behind all of it, wall to rail, and stayed shut.
pauses.reason: Reset after the final husk is dealt with; silence returns to the cut.
Pause for Rook's first question and Toren's broken response about Senna.

pauses.after: "Where are the rest of your people?" he said.
pauses.reason: Brief pause before the silence of 'Nobody answered him' lands.
